question.leadin: Answer the following about indigenous peoples of South America.
question.text: The Quechua group, who share their name with the language of the Inca Empire, live in and around this mountain range in Peru, Ecuador, and Bolivia.
question.clue: A culture in this mountain range depicted a spider called the "Decapitator" and created a mummy known as the Lord of Sipan.

swap.leadin: It is believed that this empire's capital of Cuzco was built in the shape of a puma.
swap.text: Name this Andean Empire whose inhabitants spoke Quechua and invented a system of sharing information through knots called quipu. Much was learned about this empire with the discovery of Machu Picchu.
swap.clue: This empire's capital city, Cuzco, was captured by the conquistador Francisco Pizarro.

question.leadin: One succession conflict in this empire saw Huascar executed by Atahualpa, who became Huayna Capac's successor.
question.text: Name this Realm of Four Parts centered on the city of Cusco. This Andean empire was founded by Pachacuti.
question.clue: This state kept records on a series of knotted ropes called quipus.

swap.leadin: Tupac Amaru's 1572 uprising could not reverse the fate of this empire.
swap.text: Identify this empire that was weakened by the civil war between the sons of Huayna Capac.
swap.clue: One ruler of these people allegedly gained a fortune from places termed the "Outer Belt" and the "Fire Belt," and another earned a name meaning "overturner of the world" or "earthshaker" after stones supposedly came to life to help him repel Chanka invaders.

question.text: This conquistador kidnapped and executed Atahualpa before proceeding to crush the Inca Empire. He later founded Lima, the capital of modern-day Peru.

swap.leadin: Women new to this city were sent to schools called acllahuasi ("ock-yah-WAH-see"), where they were trained to become secluded virgins who brewed chicha.
swap.text: Name this former capital that was shaped like a jaguar and built from stone without using mortar. This capital surrendered after Atalhualpa was captured at Cajamarca.
swap.clue: A chief of this puma-shaped city adopted a name roughly translated as "world turner."

question.text: This Peruvian ship sank the Esmeralda before Chile captured it in the War of the Pacific. It took its name from an Incan noble who lost a civil war to his brother Atahualpa.
question.clue: This ship participated in most major engagements in Peruvian history during the latter half of the nineteenth century. It was named for the brother of Incan ruler Atahualpa.

swap.leadin: This site was excavated by Hiram Bingham in 1911.
swap.text: Name this Peruvian archaeological site, a fortress and royal palace built during the reign of Pachacuti.
swap.clue: Hiram Bingham ("HEE-rum BING-hum") publicized the existence of this site.

question.leadin: A socialist leader with mixed descent from these people, Juan Jose Torres, was overthrown in a US backed coup d'etat led by Hugo Banzer.
question.text: Name these people whose flag is known as the Wiphala. A leader of the cocalero movement descended from these people founded the pro-indigenous MAS party.
question.clue: The katarismo movement which has sought to empower this group since the 1970s is named for the husband of martyr Bartolina Sisa.

swap.leadin: This region contains much cinnabar, which made it useful in extracting a certain precious metal through the patio process.
swap.text: Name this "mercury mountain" in a namesake region and city in Peru.
swap.clue: This Peruvian city home to a "mercury mountain" whose deposits became much more crucial after mercury-intensive silver refining processes were introduced at neighboring Potosi.

question.text: The Incas constructed tambos and qolqas along these elements of their infrastructure, which were used to great effect to relay messages by people called chasquis. The main one was the Qhapaq Nan.
question.answerHtml: Incan roads [or obvious equivalents like trails, etc.; or caminos]
question.clue: The Qhapaq Nan was the central corridor in this system, which was begun by the Wari Empire.

swap.text: The Inca used quipu to keep track of the stock of this foodstuff. Along with dried meat known as char'ki, the Inca kept reserves of these freezed-dried potatoes in case of famines.

question.text: Vilcabamba was founded by this Incan monarch. This monarch was captured by Spanish forces and imprisoned by the brothers of Francisco Pizarro before escaping and laying siege to Cusco for 10 months.

swap.text: Kidnapped Chinese workers were also kept in slave-like conditions on these Peruvian islands in order to harvest guano. Spain seized these islands in 1864, which prompted a war in which Chile and Peru fought to take them back.
swap.clue: Peruvian magnates on these islands hired blackbirders to kidnap workers to mine guano. Spain seized these islands to acquire those mines in the 1860s, but was repulsed by a coalition of South American countries.

question.text: The original "Maritime Foundations" theory was developed after the excavation of this site at the mouth of the Supe River that likely provided fish to Caral from the nearby ocean. This place is the type site of the Norte Chico.

swap.text: The Tiwanaku and this civilization centered in the Ayacucho Basin arose during the Middle Horizon period, after the decline of the Nazca. This civilization interacted with the Tiwanaku near the site of Cerro Baul, where it built a hilltop settlement.

question.text: Lying at the confluence of the Huatanay and Tullmayo rivers, it was purportedly founded by Manco Capac. Among its tourist attractions is the church of La Merced.
question.clue: This city whose Quechua name means "center."

swap.leadin: This cloud forest culture created mosaic friezes at Gran Pajaten ("pa-ha-TEN"), built cliff tombs at Revash, and produced the Laguna de Los Condores textiles.
swap.text: Name this culture that built the walled city of Kuelap in Amazonas, Peru. This culture's people were ascribed white skin by Inca chroniclers, whose reports of their ferocity inspired their nickname of "warriors of the clouds."

question.leadin: John Rick analyzed the acoustics of the central building in this place, noting that it was designed to encourage a feeling of sounds coming from every direction at once.
question.text: Identify this archaeological site in Peru, where religious rituals took place as early as 1200 BCE. The only entrance to the Old Temple at this site faced the Mosna River to the east.
question.clue: Archaeoacoustic work has suggested that the acoustics of the labyrinth at this site were designed to disorient worshippers as they were led to the Lanzon granite stele. Alberto Fujimori named a military operation after this early Peruvian site.

swap.leadin: This civilization had its capital at Chanchan, to the north of Trujillo, and its language of Quingnam has been called the "Fisherman's language."
swap.text: Name this South American civilization that arose around 900 AD, and was known for its pottery and metallurgy.
swap.clue: These people succeeded the Moche, and they ruled from their capital at Chan Chan.
